topic: Weidlich-Wilkie clearcoat transmittance coupling vs additive blowout rig
topic_zh: Weidlich-Wilkie 汽车清漆透射窗口能量耦合对比朴素加法叠层白炉过曝
scope: Deterministic Weidlich & Wilkie (EGSR 2007) / Khronos glTF KHR_materials_clearcoat transmittance-coupled layering (E_phys = F_coat + (1 - F_coat)*L_sub with n_coat = 1.50, F0 = 0.0400, L_sub = 1.0000) versus naive additive clearcoat layering (F_coat + L_sub) and 64-bounce Stokes internal reflection series across 17 incident viewing angles (theta_i in [0 deg, 80 deg]).

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating Node CPU runs after warmup. Closed-form (1 - F_coat) substrate window evaluation versus 64-bounce Stokes internal reflection series.

protocol.function: E_phys(θ_i) = F_coat + (1 − F_coat)·L_sub → 60° (0.07 + 0.93) = 1.0000 vs Additive 80° = 1.4099 (+40.99% Blowout)

robustness.name: Sampled 17 incident viewing angles strictly pass the 1.0000 White Furnace test without grazing rim blowout

good_fit: Automotive metallic basecoat + polyurethane clearcoat, lacquered wood, carbon fiber, and wet surfaces in glTF KHR_materials_clearcoat and Three.js
Attenuating substrate diffuse and metallic flakes by (1 - F_coat) so total reflectance never exceeds 1.0000
Recomputing internal substrate Fresnel from relative IOR (n_sub / n_coat) to capture wet-surface darkening
Evaluating Schlick clearcoat partition in 5 scalar multiplications without multi-bounce loops
not_for: Uncoated single-layer matte drywall or raw concrete
Nanometer soap bubbles where wave phase interference dominates (use Belcour-Barla Iridescence Round 102)
Upright velvet cloth pile (use Estevez-Kulla Charlie Sheen Round 103)
